questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the movement of particles in gases?
choices: They move in fixed positions with strong attractions.
They are closely packed and move freely in all directions.
They move past each other in a limited space.
They are completely free to move in all directions.
questions.solution: Gases have particles that are completely free to move in all directions because the interparticle attractions are negligible. The other options describe solids or liquids, which have stronger attractions and limited movement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the movement of gas particles?
choices: Smelling a flower from a distance
Seeing a stone fall to the ground
Holding a book in your hand
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Smelling a flower from a distance' because it demonstrates the movement of gas particles. When you smell a flower, the fragrance particles spread through the air, which is a gas, and reach your nose. The other options involve forces or actions that do not directly relate to the movement of gas particles. Smelling a flower is a direct example of gas particles moving through the air.

questions.stem: What are the tiny particles that make up all matter?
questions.solution: Atoms and molecules are the fundamental building blocks of all matter, as they combine to form everything around us. Cells are the basic units of living organisms, not all matter. Bacteria are living organisms, and dust particles are made up of many different substances, not the fundamental particles of matter.

questions.stem: What is the main reason why gases mix easily?
choices: They have very low interparticle forces
They have fixed shape and volume
They are always in a liquid state
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'They have very low interparticle forces.' Gases mix easily because the particles in a gas have very weak forces of attraction between them, allowing them to move freely and mix with each other. The other options are incorrect because gases do not have fixed shape or volume, they are not always in a liquid state, and their density is not the main reason for mixing.

questions.stem: If a student breaks a piece of chalk into smaller pieces and then grinds it further, what can be concluded about the particles of chalk?

They can be broken down further into smaller units

questions.solution: The process of breaking and grinding chalk shows that it can be divided into smaller parts, which supports the idea that it is made of smaller units. The correct option reflects that particles can be further divided, while the other options contradict the physical reality of matter being conserved and not changing into different types or disappearing.

questions.stem: If a student dissolves salt in water, what can be said about the particles of salt and water?

questions.stem: A student observes that when sugar is dissolved in water, the water becomes sweet. What conclusion can be drawn about the sugar particles?
choices: They are no longer present as individual particles
They are still visible to the naked eye

questions.solution: When sugar dissolves in water, it breaks into tiny particles that are too small to see but still exist, which is why the water tastes sweet. The option that they are not affected by the water is also incorrect because the water causes the sugar to spread out and dissolve.

hi.stem: एक छात्र एक प्रयोग करता है जहां एक ठोस को गर्म किया जाता है और यह एक गैस में बदल जाता है। ठोस के कणों के बारे में क्या निष्कर्ष निकाला जा सकता है?
choices: वे अधिक स्वतंत्र रूप से गति करते हैं
वे अपनी पहचान खो देते हैं
वे एक अलग पदार्थ में बदल जाते हैं
hi.solution: जब एक ठोस को गर्म किया जाता है और यह एक गैस में बदल जाता है, तो इसके कण ऊर्जा प्राप्त करते हैं और अधिक स्वतंत्र रूप से गति करते हैं, जो अवस्था में परिवर्तन की व्याख्या करता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि कण बड़े नहीं होते, अपनी पहचान नहीं खोते, या इस भौतिक प्रक्रिया में एक अलग पदार्थ में नहीं बदलते।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate scientific terminology as found in Hindi-medium textbooks.

mr.stem: एका विद्यार्थ्याने एका पदार्थाला गरम करून त्याचे वायूत बदलण्याचा प्रयोग केला. त्या ठिकाणी पदार्थाच्या कणांबद्दल काय निष्कर्ष काढता येईल?
mr.solution: जेव्हा एका घन पदार्थाला गरम केला जातो आणि तो वायूत बदलतो, तेव्हा त्याच्या कणांना ऊर्जा मिळते आणि ते जास्त स्वातंत्र्याने चालतात, जे अवस्था बदलाचे स्पष्टीकरण देते. इतर विकल्प अयोग्य आहेत कारण कण जास्त मोठे होत नाहीत, आपली ओळख गमावत नाहीत किंवा वेगळ्या पदार्थात बदलत नाहीत या भौमितिक प्रक्रियेदरम्यान.
